# MCP-server config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/mcp-servers/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.MCPServerBlock` — the **legacy** pre-register-once gateway block, declaring one server by `mode`: `pass-through` (a single far-side `endpoint`) or `aggregate` (a set of `member` blocks merged into one catalog). The block label is the server name.

**Superseded by `mcp_upstream` + `mcp_exposure` (ADR-062 §2)** and retained only while callers migrate: register a backing server once as an `mcp_upstream`, then expose it independent or aggregate as one or more `mcp_exposure`s. This block declares **no virtual MCP server** — a virtual server is a `type = "virtual"` `mcp_upstream` backed by a `capability_group`.

| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `inventory` — the block label is the identity; the file is a container and its stem carries no meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `mcp_server` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/mcp-servers/<name>.hcl` |

## Example

A minimal `mcp-servers`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/mcp-servers/example-mcp-server.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

mcp_server "example-mcp-server" {
  mode     = "pass-through"
  endpoint = "https://example.internal"
}
```

## `auth_far_side` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | — | — | — | The far-side scheme: bearer or oauth (service modes, one credential the gateway holds for every caller), or connection (each caller's own credential, selected from the delegated-token vault by the connection named below). The retired per-person spellings user_delegated and user_token no longer load (ADR-148 D2; see docs/ops/upgrade-to-connections.md). |
| `connection` | string | no | — | — | — | Required for type = connection, refused otherwise: the .tera/connections/<name>.hcl this upstream acts through. The connection declares how a person obtains the credential - by consent through its oauth block, by pasting through its token block, or either - so the upstream carries no registration of its own. Several upstreams may name one connection; a person who connected it once is attached on all of them. |
| `authorization_server` | string | no | — | — | — | Retired: never valid. An inline per-person OAuth registration is refused at load naming ADR-148 D2 and docs/ops/upgrade-to-connections.md; declare it on a connection's oauth block instead. |

| `token_url` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `client_id` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `client_secret` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `scope` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
